notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: I read the complete held EO 11261 (30 FR 15397, Dec. 11, 1965): its only operative text substitutes a new sec. 304 in EO 10973 (administration of foreign assistance): (a) the United States Information Agency performs all public information functions abroad for foreign-assistance programs; (b) the USIA Director is delegated the President's functions under FAA secs. 221 and 222 as they relate to informational media guaranties under sec. 1011 of the USIEEA 1948. It has no own term, no savings clause, and no life apart from EO 10973. I read the complete held EO 12163 (44 FR 56673, Sept. 29, 1979): sec. 1-903(a)(1) provides 'The following are revoked: (1) Executive Order No. 10973 of November 3, 1961, as amended', with no exception; sec. 1-905 makes it effective Oct. 1, 1979; sec. 1-504 re-establishes the public-information function in the International Communication Agency (USIA's successor name), which is the counterpart of new sec. 304(a). The by-name revocation of the parent 'as amended' removes the sec. 304 that EO 11261 substituted. D6 self-check, every later event: EO 11417 (adds a Commerce member to the Development Loan Committee in sec. 305), EO 11685, EO 11816, EO 11959 and EO 12118 amend other parts of EO 10973 and none touches sec. 304 or revives it; EO 11579 sec. 2(d) supersedes EO 10973 only insofar as inconsistent (partial) and its sec. 2(a) is itself revoked by 12163 sec. 1-903(a)(2), so it is not an ending of this order but also does not revive it. Open point I could not close from held sources: EO 12163 does not re-delegate the FAA secs. 221-222 informational-media-guaranty functions of sec. 304(b), and sec. 1-904 continues 'delegations ... made with respect to any function affected by this order and not revoked' until amended. I read 1-904 as a transition clause for implementing actions that is subordinate to the express revocation in 1-903(a)(1) (otherwise every delegation in EO 10973 would survive its own revocation); the status of the underlying FAA sections is not in the held record. That reading, and the possibility that sec. 304(b) lingered, is flagged for the reviewer. No earlier own-term ending exists. Provisional NO hypothesis only.
